prose.title: Real Deal Creel Spent the Most, Churned the Most, and Leads Its Division on Paper
prose.dek: Keith Creelman spent {{f.team.0008.auction_spend}} across both auctions, more than any owner, landed Puka Nacua in the summer's three-way, and made {{f.team.0008.pickups_s3}} waiver pickups before week one. The preseason simulation ranks Real Deal Creel {{f.team.0008.power_rank|ord}}, and first in Maddie Mondays.

paragraphs: April was a teardown. Creelman carried {{f.team.0008.active_roster_opening}} active players and just {{f.team.0008.cap_opening}} in salary, the smallest commitment in the league, and one top-twelve starter, Dallas Goedert at tight end. Tetairoa McMillan was solid. The {{f.team.0008.holes_opening}} holes were Deshaun Watson at quarterback, TreVeyon Henderson and Emanuel Wilson at running back, Christian Watson at receiver, Marvin Harrison Jr and Trey Benson in the flexes, and Keon Coleman in the superflex.

The first big move came in April. Kenneth Walker, the largest contract he moved all year at {{f.team.0008.biggest_contract_traded_away}} a year, went to HammerTime for their 2027 first. Blake Watson came off the taxi squad at no cost. Two rookie deals ran out: Emanuel Wilson went to Blake Bombers at the Expired Rookie Auction and Jalen Carter was let go.

t.0008.slot_bridge.title: April: who held each priced slot

paragraphs: Draft week he sent 1.04 to Gride for 1.07 and Travis Etienne, whom Gride had tagged two days earlier, then moved around the second and third rounds and made {{f.team.0008.rookie_picks_count}} picks: KC Concepcion at 1.07, a slot that has produced a usable player more often than not, Omar Cooper Jr. at 1.09, De'Zhaun Stribling, Sonny Styles and Zion Young. He was the busiest buyer at the Expired Rookie Auction too, {{f.team.0008.era_lots_won}} players for {{f.team.0008.era_spend}}: Chris Rodriguez, Kayshon Boutte, Michael Mayer, Kendre Miller and Will McDonald.

Then he made room. In July he cut Noah Fant ({{f.team.0008.cut_14137_salary}} of salary, a {{f.team.0008.cut_14137_penalty}} penalty), Trey Benson ({{f.team.0008.cut_16594_salary}}, {{f.team.0008.cut_16594_penalty}}) and Keon Coleman ({{f.team.0008.cut_16617_salary}}, {{f.team.0008.cut_16617_penalty}}), and in the three-way with C-Town and Blake Bombers he sent McMillan, his own 2027 first, Rodriguez and Omar Cooper for Puka Nacua, an Elite WR1, moving {{f.team.0008.trade5_salary_out}} of salary out and {{f.team.0008.trade5_salary_in}} in. The first-round pick he gave up was his own; the one Walker bought, HammerTime's, is still his. He went into the auction with {{f.team.0008.active_roster_preauction}} active players and {{f.team.0008.cap_preauction}} committed.

t.0008.moves_s2.title: From the draft to the auction lock

paragraphs: Then he spent more than anyone. At the Free Agent Auction it was {{f.team.0008.faa_spend}} on {{f.team.0008.faa_lots_won}} players: Dak Prescott for {{f.team.0008.faa_12620_price}} after fifteen bids, Saquon Barkley for {{f.team.0008.faa_13604_price}}, Kyler Murray for {{f.team.0008.faa_14056_price}}, and Jacoby Brissett, Blake's July cut, for {{f.team.0008.faa_12616_price}} as insurance.

What it bought: Prescott and Barkley, the two Very good buys, and Murray, the Good one, in the superflex. His offense gained the third-most at the auction, {{f.team.0008.faa_off_gain_rank|ord}} of {{f.league.teams}}, and the league table ranks the money {{f.team.0008.faa_off_rank|ord}} for what each dollar added, right at the league average.

Then the churn. {{f.team.0008.pickups_s3}} waiver pickups before week one, more than anyone, most of them one-for-one swaps at the back of the roster, and Trey Benson among them, claimed back less than three weeks after he was cut. The multi-year contracts came in September: Parker Washington at {{f.team.0008.contract_16192_salary}} this year and {{f.team.0008.contract_16192_tcv}} in all, Chig Okonkwo at {{f.team.0008.contract_15889_salary}} and {{f.team.0008.contract_15889_tcv}}, both front-loaded, plus the two Expired Rookie Auction buys and four waiver pickups. Nacua's deal was restructured and put back the same week, a temporary {{f.team.0008.restructure_room_freed}} of room, and Deshaun Watson was cut with a {{f.team.0008.cut_13113_penalty}} penalty charged to 2027. He sits at {{f.team.0008.cap_current_room}} of room.

The lineup it built has {{f.team.0008.studs_today}} top-twelve starters, Prescott, Barkley, Nacua and Goedert, with Etienne and Murray solid, and {{f.team.0008.holes_today}} holes: Christian Watson at receiver and Parker Washington and TreVeyon Henderson in the flexes. The defense is a footnote, as always, but the work behind it is not: he has acquired {{f.team.0008.idp_adds_alltime}} defenders since 2010, the most in the league, and led it in that for {{f.team.0008.idp_adds_lead_streak}} straight seasons.

captions.t.0008.faa_value: Ranked by how much each owner's starting offense improved between the auction lock and the close, for every dollar he spent on quarterbacks, backs, receivers and tight ends at the Free Agent Auction. What it bought sorts those buys by grade at their position: Elite, Very good, Good or Depth.

paragraphs: Creelman has been here since {{f.team.0008.hist_first_season}}, all {{f.team.0008.hist_seasons}} completed seasons, and the record has one gap that everyone in the league knows about: {{f.team.0008.hist_playoffs}} playoff trips, {{f.team.0008.hist_div_titles}} division titles, runner-up finishes in {{f.team.0008.hist_runner_up_years}}, and no title. His career all-play record is {{f.team.0008.hist_allplay_pct}}.

Maddie Mondays holds two owners with two titles each, and the simulation picks the one without a title to win it: Real Deal Creel is {{f.team.0008.power_rank|ord}} in the league with a {{f.team.0008.sim_p_division}} chance at the division and {{f.team.0008.sim_p_title}} title odds, Sex Manther {{f.league.power_rank_0007|ord}}, and L.A. Looks {{f.league.power_rank_0001|ord}}. Josh Martel won in {{f.league.title_years_0007}} and Ryan Bousquet in {{f.league.title_years_0001}}, and Creelman plays each of them five times.

the next three years, as the owner would type them.... 2027.... the first title haha. the commissioner reviews the result, cites precedent, rules it valid, and shrugs. 2028.... a repeat, celebrated with a keystone light and a winamp playlist nobody asked for lol. 2029.... he lists the franchise for sale, gets no offers, and wins it again anyway haha
Week one has barely started for Real Deal Creel: with {{f.league.wk_teams_final}} NFL teams done, Nacua has all {{f.team.0008.wk_points_final}} of his points so far.
